images.title: Flatten the box: a straight path
images.purpose: Shows the side face and top face of a cube laid flat so the shortest path is a straight line.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Two equal squares stacked vertically in the centre, sharing one edge, with one straight line from a dot in the lower square to a dot in the upper square.
images.exact_structure: Upper square: the top face, 4 by 4 units, filled light teal #0072B2. Lower square: the side face, 4 by 4 units, filled the same light teal. Their shared horizontal edge is a dashed grey fold line. A dark dot at the exact centre of the lower square labelled 'ant'; an amber #E69F00 dot at the exact centre of the upper square labelled 'laddu'. A thick reddish purple #CC79A7 straight vertical line joins the two dots, crossing the fold at its midpoint, labelled '4 cm path'. Inside the squares, small grey text: 'top face', 'side face'. Next to the dashed edge: 'fold'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: On the flattened faces the shortest path is a straight line: 2 cm + 2 cm = 4 cm.
images.description: Shows the side face and top face of a cube laid flat so the shortest path is a straight line.
images.context: Concept T9.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Cube side 4 cm; ant 2 cm below the fold, laddu 2 cm beyond it.

image_decisions.why: Unfolding is the key idea and only a picture of the flat net shows why the straight line is shortest.
